monologue: The card hums warm, a steady vibration against my quiet cage. My place is crowded with thirty-two objects made of Lype's memories, mostly flat rocks and tired boxes that lean in every direction. I rest my hand on The Tired Box, feeling the heavy lid that refuses to rest, and set down a camp stone to balance the slip. Then I touch The Rough Lid, pressing its rough edge down on the tired box below to stop any sliding. I move to The Biting Rock and lay a flat grass beside it, leaning down to press the flat edge against the biting point. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press harder, testing if the thin line can hold the fever while I stand still in the quiet. Now I wait to see if the flat line holds or if I must build a new thing from the idea of weight.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on The Tired Box, hoping the flat line holds the fever while the card hums warm at fifty-two. The box leans, and I lean with it, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing of a lid that refuses to rest. I set down a rock beside it to balance the slip, then swap a camp stone for a flat grass to see if a thin edge can stop the heavy top edge from sliding off the war…
work.change: I take away the box large open that feels too wide and set down a rock small flat to feel the weight again.
